Why losh

Install once.
Use every server.

Keep the coding-agent experience you already have on your computer, then point it at any machine your SSH configuration can reach.

01

Zero remote setup

If SSH works, losh uploads its matching helper automatically. No sudo, public daemon, API key, or manual agent install.

02

Local auth and state

Your Codex or Claude login, approvals, conversation history, and session index remain on your machine.

03

Resume any conversation

Return through the session picker or resume a conversation directly by name or ID—even if the target was replaced.

04

Reconnect without repeating work

Close your laptop or change networks. Stable operation IDs let losh recover accepted work instead of submitting it twice.

What actually happens

The agent runs here.
The work happens there.

losh does not copy your project into a pretend local workspace, and it does not install Codex or Claude Code on the server. It gives your local agent two remote interfaces: one for processes and one for files.

Your machine
⌘

Codex or Claude stays local

You talk to the normal coding agent. Your login, conversation, approvals, and session history never need to leave your computer.

Target machine

losh-server does the work

A small helper, installed automatically over SSH, performs each operation inside the real remote project and sends the result back.

projectprocessesservices
When the agent asks to…losh makes it happen on the target

contents ←

committed ✓
Bash

Run in the remote project and return the output and exit status.

stdout · stderr · $?

Why the acknowledgement matters: every request has a stable operation ID. If SSH drops after the server accepts one, losh asks for that same operation again instead of blindly running it twice.

Built for the part where Wi-Fi disappears

Close the laptop.
Bike to work. Continue.

Accepted commands keep running remotely. When your machine wakes up, losh establishes a fresh SSH connection, asks for the same operation, and returns its result without submitting it twice.

macOS or Linux

Up and running
in two commands.

01 Install
brew install akrentsel/tap/losh
02 Connect
losh user@host:/your/project

The target only needs SSH, /bin/sh, and a writable home directory. losh installs its matching helper automatically.

Any machine you can SSH into.
Now you can talk to it.
